janet (Support): FYI customer opened an escalation — their integration is failing when they enable strict structured output. They set response_format: "json" + strict: true. Sometimes the API returns a 200 with an HTML error page body which causes their JSON parser to blow up. Logged request_id: req_0a1b2c3d. Happened ~5x in last 30m, started after today's model rollout.

janet (Support): customer sample (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_*REDACTED*" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "Accept: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-std-2.1","input":"...","response_format":"json","strict":true}'
```

redwood-bot: deploy-bot rolled out model open-std-2.1 -> v2.1 to hosted/us-west-2 at 2026-02-01T12:07:00Z

tom (Eng): thanks. Can you paste the exact raw response body they received for req_0a1b2c3d? Need headers and body to confirm content-type mismatch. Also which route were they hitting (hosted API or dedicated)?

janet (Support): pasted raw response (customer redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

<html>
<head><title>Error</title></head>
<body>Unhandled exception: NullReference at runtime...</body>
</html>
```

priya (SRE): I'm seeing an upstream 500 in runtime logs for req_0a1b2c3d during the rollout window. Gateway preserved upstream Content-Type (text/html) and returned 200 to client (our gateway will sometimes rewrite status). The body is an HTML error page from the model runtime fallback handler.

priya (SRE): log snippet (ingress):
```
[2026-02-01T12:09:22Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d upstream_status=500 upstream_ct=text/html route=/v1/generate handler=runtime-fallback msg="runtime exception, emitting error page"
[2026-02-01T12:09:22Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d gateway_status=200 gateway_ct=text/html
```

mike (DevEx): likely cause: when response_format=json and strict=true we assume backend provides JSON + app/json header. If a runtime error occurs and the error middleware returns an HTML page, the gateway currently passes that through without converting to a json error object — so client sees HTML despite expecting JSON and strict enforcement fails on client side.

mike (DevEx): quick repro (local):
```bash
# simulate runtime error page + wrong content-type
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-std-2.1","response_format":"json","strict":true}' -D - \
  --resolve api.redwood.ai:8080:127.0.0.1
# Expect: gateway should return JSON error {"error":...} with Content-Type: application/json
```

tom (Eng): Confirmed. Runtime error handler sets text/html in a few code paths (legacy). Patch plan: 1) ensure gateway canonicalizes error responses to JSON when request asked for structured output; 2) add a lint/test to catch content-type drift for structured routes; 3) backfill a hotfix to convert HTML error pages to {"error":"internal","details":"..."} with app/json for the hosted API.

tom (Eng): Assigning to eng-runtime on-call for hotfix. Also need to surface a graceful fallback to non-strict mode for clients that want resilience.

priya (SRE): I've added a temporary router rule that intercepts responses with content-type text/html on /v1/generate and replaces body with a minimal JSON error and sets Content-Type: application/json for matching requests. Rule pushed to us-west-2. Monitoring for recurrence.

janet (Support): Updated customer: suggested immediate workaround is set strict:false OR use client-side wrapper to catch HTML body and retry, but they prefer platform fix. Customer appreciated the quick mitigation and asked for ETA for permanent fix.

mike (DevEx): I'll produce a small repro script and a CI test to prevent regressions. Also adding an alert for any future responses where request had response_format=json but gateway_ct != application/json.

tom (Eng): ETA for hotfix: ~2h, then full rollout with tests tomorrow. I'll open an internal ticket and post PR link here when ready.

janet (Support): Thanks — please ping when deployed so I can confirm with the customer and close the escalation. :thumbsup:

redwood-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-1073 (structured-output content-type drift)

mike (DevEx): I'll attach repro and add to postmortem once resolved.

tom (Eng): follow-up action items: [eng-runtime patch], [CI test], [monitoring alert], [customer follow-up]. Assigning owners in the ticket.

priya (SRE): monitoring shows no new occurrences in the last 20 minutes after the router rule. Closing temporary mitigation after hotfix verifies.

janet (Support): closing loop with customer now, will reopen if they see more.
